original_defect: The isometry identity is true, but a zero output cannot be normalized; a k-row column isometry need not give k positive-weight components. More seriously, infinitely many isometries do not imply distinct physical ensembles, since row phases/permutations and zero padding can preserve the physical ensemble.

substantive_reconstruction.complex_index_identity: For u_l=sqrt(p_l)psi_l and w_j=sum_l V_jl u_l, the coefficient of |u_l><u_m| in sum_j|w_j><w_j| is sum_j V_jl conjugate(V_jm)=(V^dagger V)_(m,l)=delta_ml. Thus the result is exactly sum_l|u_l><u_l|=rho, including complex V. There is no transpose-versus-adjoint substitution.
substantive_reconstruction.zero_outputs_and_normalization: q_j=||w_j||^2>=0 and sum_jq_j=tr(rho)=1. Positive q_j gives a unit phi_j=w_j/sqrt(q_j). If q_j=0, definiteness gives w_j=0; delete that contribution or assign its zero weight any unit vector, which exists for a nonzero mixed-state Hilbert support. At most k positive terms is the correct general conclusion. An appended zero row makes the missing case explicit without a new premise.
substantive_reconstruction.noninjectivity: If D is diagonal unitary on output labels, DV is another column isometry and w_j only acquires its row phase, preserving q_j and the rank-one projector. Permuting rows only reorders terms; zero rows and duplicate rays add descriptions. This disproves the predecessor's automatic injectivity step, not the true nonuniqueness theorem.
substantive_reconstruction.mixed_state_witness_and_continuity: A mixed finite density state has rank s>=2 and two strictly positive eigenvalues lambda1,lambda2. On their orthonormal eigenvectors put u=sqrt(lambda1)e1,v=sqrt(lambda2)e2. The stated rotation is orthogonal, hence a column isometry, and w1,w2 have the two displayed strictly positive weights. On0<theta<pi/4, w1's e2/e1 ratio is sqrt(lambda2/lambda1)tan(theta)>0 and strictly increasing; w2 has negative ratio. No row phase can alter these ratios; w1 cannot match w2 or an untouched orthogonal eigenvector ray. Thus distinct angles yield distinct unordered weighted projector ensembles, even when lambda1=lambda2. This independently proves infinitely many ensembles of each rho and therefore alternatives to any one initial ensemble.
substantive_reconstruction.longer_isometry: The displayed first column(1/sqrt2,1/2,-1/2) and second column(0,1/sqrt2,1/sqrt2) have squared norms1 and inner product0. Add s-2 disjoint identity rows/columns to obtain(s+1)-by-s V with V^dagger V=I. The three weights are lambda1/2 and twice(lambda1/4+lambda2/2), summing to lambda1+lambda2, all strictly positive. The first output lies on e1; the other two have nonzero v coefficients and opposite u coefficients, so their rays are pairwise distinct and cannot be untouched spectral rays. This is a genuine length increase over the rank-s spectral ensemble, not an assertion that every k>r or every initial list automatically lengthens.
